chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn, from al-Naḍr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Saʿīd al-Aʿraj, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the nafilah prayer on Friday,
So he said: Sixteen rakʿahs before al-ʿaṣr.
Then he said: And ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: Whatever is added is better.
And he said: If a man wishes, he may perform six rakʿahs of it in the early part of the day, and six rakʿahs in the middle of the day, and pray al-ẓuhr, then pray four of it, then pray al-ʿaṣr.

key_terms.سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً: sixteen units of prayer prescribed here as the Friday nafilah
key_terms.صَدْرِ النَّهَارِ: the early part of the day
key_terms.صَلَاةِ النَّافِلَةِ: the recommended supererogatory prayer being discussed
key_terms.قَبْلَ الْعَصْرِ: before the ʿaṣr prayer, indicating the time frame
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day on which this prayer arrangement applies

ai.seo_question: How should the Friday nafilah prayer be performed and divided before al-ʿaṣr?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the recommended nafilah prayer on Friday, stating that it consists of sixteen rakʿahs before al-ʿaṣr. It also indicates flexibility in how these rakʿahs may be distributed throughout the day, and conveys that increasing voluntary prayer is better.
